memories.author: patient
memories.text: I have been having crampy abdominal pain and bloating after meals for the past few months, sometimes relieved by passing gas. I also get throbbing headaches on one side, lasting a few hours, with nausea. I work as a florist and stand for long hours. I take over‑the‑counter antispasmodics occasionally but they do not help much. I would like a review of my symptoms and advice on long‑term management.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Review of IBS and migraine symptoms.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Crampy lower abdominal pain, bloating, occasional diarrhoea; episodic unilateral throbbing headache with photophobia and nausea.
EXAMINATION: Abdomen soft, non‑tender, no masses. Blood pressure 118/72 mmHg, weight 58 kg, BMI 22.9 (normal). Neurological exam normal.
IMPRESSION: Irritable bowel syndrome, predominantly mixed pattern. Migraine, episodic, well controlled on current prophylaxis.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS. Continue propranolol 40 mg OD for migraine prevention, sumatriptan 50 mg SOS, topiramate 25 mg HS, naproxen 500 mg SOS. Order CBC, stool routine, tTG‑IgA. Return if: worsening abdominal pain, vomiting, blood in stool, headache with fever >39°C, visual changes, or weakness.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Mebeverine 135 mg tablet – take one tablet twice daily.
Ispaghula husk 5 g sachet – take one sachet once daily with water.
Loperamide 2 mg capsule – take one capsule after loose stool, max 8 mg/day.
Propranolol 40 mg tablet – take one tablet once daily.
Sumatriptan 50 mg tablet – take one tablet at migraine onset, repeat after 2 hours if needed, max 200 mg/24h.
Topiramate 25 mg tablet – take one tablet at bedtime.
Naproxen 500 mg tablet – take one tablet after food, max 1 g/day, SOS.

memories.author: lab
memories.text:
Hemoglobin 13.2 g/dl (12-16), WBC 6.4 x10^9/l (4-10), Platelets 215 x10^9/l (150-400).
Stool routine: Ova and parasites nil, pus cells 0-2/hpf, RBC nil.
tTG‑IgA: <2 U/ml (negative <7).

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Neurological examination performed. Patient alert, oriented. Cranial nerves II‑XII intact. Muscle strength 5/5 bilaterally. Tone normal. Reflexes 2+ symmetric. Sensation intact to light touch and pinprick. Gait steady. No pronator drift. No dysmetria. No nystagmus. Findings consistent with a normal neurological exam.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: CT head (non‑contrast) performed. No acute intracranial hemorrhage, infarct, or mass lesion. Ventricular system and sulci normal. No evidence of chronic ischemic changes. Report: Normal study.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Follow‑up on IBS and migraine.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Abdominal bloating reduced, occasional loose stools after fatty meals. Headache frequency down to 1‑2 per month, mild, responsive to sumatriptan.
EXAMINATION: Abdomen soft, mild tenderness in left lower quadrant. BP 120/74, weight 59 kg, BMI 23.1 (overweight per Asian cut‑off).
IMPRESSION: IBS symptoms improved but still triggered by diet. Migraine well controlled. BMI overweight – advise diet and activity.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS. Continue propranolol 40 mg OD, topiramate 25 mg HS; stop naproxen SOS due to GI irritation, replace with paracetamol 500 mg SOS if needed. Reinforce low‑FODMAP diet, regular walks 30 min daily. Return if: worsening pain, vomiting, blood in stool, headache with neurological deficit, or BP >160/100.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Review of IBS, migraine and cardiovascular risk.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Occasional abdominal discomfort after festive meals, no diarrhoea. Headaches rare, only mild tension‑type.
EXAMINATION: Abdomen non‑tender. BP 122/76, weight 60 kg, BMI 23.8 (overweight).
IMPRESSION: IBS stable. Migraine infrequent. Lipids within target, glucose normal. Overweight persists – reinforce lifestyle.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current IBS and migraine meds. Advise Mediterranean‑style diet, aerobic activity 150 min/week, weight goal 5‑7% reduction. Return if: severe abdominal pain, vomiting, blood in stool, new neurologic symptoms, chest pain, or dyspnea on exertion.

memories.author: front_desk

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Routine follow‑up.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: No abdominal pain or bloating for past month. Headaches absent.
EXAMINATION: Abdomen soft, non‑tender. BP 119/73, weight 58 kg, BMI 22.4 (normal).
IMPRESSION: IBS in remission. Migraine absent. Weight normal – commend lifestyle efforts.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue mebeverine 135 mg BD, ispaghula husk 5 g OD, loperamide 2 mg SOS. Continue propranolol 40 mg OD, topiramate 25 mg HS. Paracetamol SOS as needed. Reinforce maintenance diet and activity. Return if: abdominal pain, vomiting, blood in stool, headache with neurologic signs, chest pain, or breathlessness.
